Close to campus, no pool, gym, free printing

submissions.note: Friend owned the condominium. Good Courtyard, it's a bit of a walk like 20min from Campus
used google maps to find the location, just called the place. Various spacious but no laundry, but can accommodate my family when they come over
I signed as a 9 month lease cause I didn't want to pay over the summer
The cellings are very high and one of the rooms has a downtown view
One time payment of $200 for utlities. Enjoy the single just think the price is a little high
Wanted to do quarters but they raised their prices and everything else was running out so 2215 had an opening. Currently in the only double Occupancy room with someone
Window fee was $30 a month, close by campus and everyone was living there
Rooms decent, but it's cheap and random roomates
Roommates wanted to sign and so just follower. Really like how fancy it was with nice study rooms and it being clean with a gym too!
Double occupancy with 4 people in the house, only thing is sharing a bathroom can be difficult
Includes amenity fee's and window fee's. They decreased my rent from last year by around $100! Still double occupancy

I’ve heard about co-ops from a friend, then I looked them up and researched them myself.. It’s good for the price you pay, but don’t expect anything luxurious. I’m happy with having my own room and sharing a bathroom with my roommate, but it’s definitely not anything fancy and you’ll have to do labor to keep the co-op running (cooking, cleaning, etc). It's also only $335 for the whole year! and food is included in the price!
Searching around wampus. Average wampus apartment, Older style interior but space is a lot. Kitchen could be bigger. Maintenance is responsive and elevator is quick and fast.
No. Zillow.. Dryer takes a little longer to dry and it is north university.
Research. I like it personally. If you live on the inside it’s depressing
Heard utilities were on the expensive side and they low key are
Just signed for next year so I've only toured but it still looks good!
It's alright but the water is a little funky
I like having my own bathroom, it's also just a 5min walk from the CPE
Pet fees, and pest fees. Updated furniture, and painted walls
Haven't moved in yet! signed for 2026 fall!
Realtor. No hidden fees. complex is always dirty and management is annoying 😹
it was the cheapest option at the time and I just followed my friend cause he wanted me to room with him. It's similar to Castilian and like I've heard their quite good with maintenance
Google Maps. No fees.. Circuit breaks, but calm otherwise

Scoured around the internet! No hidden fees (just read the contract carefully). I really like my experience overall. Only downside is that mold grows and in one particular bathroom, it’s genuinely horrible (the smell, how fast mold grows, etc)
I like my place, but I think I also just have a really good unit. I have a small room (with balcony), but my roommates have ginormous room
I found it from advertising but no hidden fees. It’s pretty okay not luxury living but a good apartment for a good price. With some decorations you can make it really nice!
UT Realtor we had a $80 amenity fee once we first moved in. Things break here a lot maintenance is good but annoying putting in a request weekly
Sublease. So far it’s pretty nice but sacrificing distance by walking more to campus.
Roomate, 70 bonus fee for paying with card. Pretty spacious
i found through website. no hidden fees. super thin walls, always smells weird bc the trash room overflows, brand new appliances and furniture but really bad quality
just google, it’s technically 1500 w rebate. fine not crazy nice

I waited until last minute to sign. Rent was originally $1200 but I got that rate, if I had waited until summer there was a promo for the other rooms in my unit for $800. Good overall, quick maintenance, however there is slight roach problem
Friend. Turning on the AC costs a lot because it’s an older unit. It’s open to the public so it’s a little less safe than an apt. It’s pretty quiet though.
N/A. Amazing, although elevators occasionally have had issues + gym treadmills
Nope. Nice bathroom, smaller apartment size and kitchen but new appliances make up for it
Word of mouth; no hidden fees just utilities were higher than I thought. Good living conditions, rooms are great just a little tax

student housing agent. I have enjoyed living here for three years, however I’ve been blessed to not have as many issues as other tenants. Management is not the best and there is no transparency when incidents occur in the complex. Although they’ve had multiple inspections for the fire alarms, they’ve all been preceded by incidents where things were not up to code. I also had a pest issue from the first day I moved in and it took two and a half years for them to resolve.
housing scout. older building, 1b1s don’t get in unit laundry
Been there for 3 years and the first time I lived there it was like 1100
They usually give out a 600$ Signing bonus. Living here was Double Occupancy, lived there for 3 Years
Yea it's fine but the location is really great
My mom found it but a previous person in my org lived there. The place is nice and close but there are some bugs. We did once have a roach problem
moved from Quarters Sterling cause they raised prices for me by $90. I don't like the stairs but there's only stairs on the entrance facing campus. Taking the elevator is an extra block on walking
They kept increasing the price by $90 every year I resigned. The study rooms were nice just a little loud cause of the CO-op (a lot of courtyard parties)
I lived there in a 4by4 and then signed in early september to get smart housing the next year.. Lobby is very messy on the weekends
Google and yes. Poor internet service, random room checks, no gym

I found it on Google :). Lowkey there is a small $10 ish dollar fee/mo to build your credit, as well as a mitigated risk fee each month if you don't have a co-signer.. Huge rooms, furniture optional ($), maintenance is quick, refurbished a year ago
Subleasing on UT off campus housing website. Relatively older appliances, 3rd floor walk up
Maintenance is very responsive, elevators though are down on a monthly basis
Friends were looking a roommate.. It's a house in the North Loop area and is a few blocks away from the Intramural Fields.
No windows in bedrooms except for 1 (extra 50 dollar per month fee).
Google Maps. Signing fees and Administrative fees. Old building terribly maintained. Only the front desk area is renovated and looks nice. The building is disgusting and loud because of the alley.
Google maps and apartment.com. It's not bad, but for the price it's great and you can definitely make it home

No hidden fees that I know of, but a larger rent concession was given two days after I signed💀. It’s a new building so the amenities and just building as a whole are really nice. Amenities I’d say are among the best in Wampus but the apartment layouts are lowkey ugly and an ineffective use of space for such a modern building.

Found on my own. No hidden fees but must ask about separate utility prices.. Smaller, slightly older studio. Have broken utility problems every once in a while but maintenance is quick. Relatively quiet area and nice space for one person

Found it via Zillow or Apartments.com or something like that. No hidden fees. Pretty nice! Well-maintained, and maintenance responds quickly. Not a sleek new apartment complex, more of a cozy vibe. My fav parts: secure gated complex, soundproof walls, and a nice little courtyard with grills and ping pong! Worst part: water is metered across the whole building and averaged, which can rack up depending on neighbors and also maintenance activities
My room was converted into a bathroom so I have to share the upstair connected bathroom
the parking just keeps increasing for no reason when I first signed it was only 150. Not crazy fancy but the space is fairly big and my room even had a balcony
I have a balcony and the room is pretty big
My bathroom isn't connected to my room but it's not that bad, I think the price is good

They have a bunch of random fee's like trash and boiler fee's and random stuff that get's tacked on for no reason. Our living room is pretty big but the actual bedroom is alright (not too big) everything is just alright. View is suppppper bad tho like I just face a wall
Strict fees regarding move out and change room fee, no matter when including renewal. It’s okay, and the people u get picked are really random
A friend, no hidden fees. I’m sharing my 1 bedroom with my girlfriend so we split, but still a good deal for around 800

Word of mouth. No hidden fees!. Good. We have our own cafe. Safety is not taken seriously. Maintenance is relatively fast. We have to wait 3 hrs to pick up packages, inconvenient when it’s an emergency.
Owned by the University. No hidden fees at all.. Really great, 24 hr desk, maintenance is always super fast, rooms and whole apt pretty spacious.

Apt locator. Initially had a roach problem that has been fixed, parking included, solid place and quiet surroundings, super spacious 1x1, HOA could be better with the property but maintenance is typically super quick

Found just by browsing Google, no hidden fees. Apartment room flooded, heat didn't work for awhile, water heater broke and wasn't fixed for a week, BRAND NEW water heater only works for 10 mins at a time + not at the same time as roommate, can't use the oven without the smoke detector going off constantly, gnat infestation for a month, apartment hallways can be fully accessed by anyone because of multiple unlocked doors, can hear the parking garage gate beep and whir with every open/close
Management is lowkey annoying. Maintenance doesn’t knock on room doors before entering and
The usual events and stuff fee. Pretty standard each room is the same size and has a window but only one room with connected bathroom

Security deposit was like 200$ also its 1240 in 12 installments but if u move out u only live there 11 months. Honestly I got such a good deal… super clean, quiet, good amenities, decent elevators, nice study room
Great building, close to mccombs, quiet residents for the most part, also next to MLK for easy access

You have to pay like 200 something to even apply so if you apply you should be set on living there. Roach infestation when we moved in, elevator is broken and they are not planning on fixing it bc they are broke, redid entire lobby for no reason (maybe this is where the money went), bitchy management (basically tried to pin the roach issue on us when they knew about it before we moved in and did not tell us)
I am subleaseing so mine is cheaper than usual. no issues so far

Found a deal online. You have to pay $15 in housing insurance and they automatically enroll you in some annoying corporate partnerships that charge you, but you can get out of it, just have to go through the hassle of removing yourself through the company.. Some of the floors have random divots or bumps, living room kinda small for how much I’m paying, front office is HORRIBLE at getting anything done. Also this is the no window price, window is $50 more I think. Had problems with the water but they fixed it (lowkey hella annoyed cause they only gave $200 in recomp to me but some people got 3 months rent???)
We didn’t have hot water for a week

They do lots of promotions like 100 off rent every month . I havnt had any hidden fees all my stuff is tracked with meters. Pretty good, bad ratings are from nasty residents who obviously attract roaches but if your clean then no roach.
Referred by a friend. Pro: Pretty clean and no mold issues .Con: elevators break down sometimes and sucky water pressure
Referred by someone, everything is a hidden fee. Spacious and decent but not worth pro w

Knew friends that already lived there and liked it.Got $10 extra hidden fee every month  when we signed for no reason. Management is nice, living rooms are big, all rooms have windows, all 4x3 have exterior windows, gym and pool are kinda meh but worth it for rent price, SUPER close to campus like  ideal location, have pillars in a lot of floor plans which is not the best but u get cheaper rent if its in ur room, shared bathrooms are nice and big
Green fee, premium floor fee, they charge more if the trash room is overfilled even if it wasn’t you. Thin walls
Mls. Nice just loud on the first floor
Fine, just a far walk- frat across the street is loud at times
Green fe application fees. Really small rooms and living room just not useful
Old building, good management, overpriced, undersized amenities. good for me on 3rd floor, lower floor deals with roaches and other issues
Maintenance got stuff done quickly. This was a semester lease only august- December so rent was a little more I’m assuming.

500 deposit for parking but you get it back. Not a clean or modern apartment-style place. It kind of looks like a prison, but when you make it your own, it works out. It's the definition of “at least you have a head to rest”. You're required to do two hours of labor in order to live here. Labor includes: taking care of plants, cleaning walkways, cleaning elevators, cleaning the laundry room, etc. The CO-OP has 3 sections, which is why we're called the Super Co-op. The first and second floors are Laurel, the third is Nueces, and the fourth and fifth are Halstead. Nueces is the only section of the building where rooms have their own kitchen, and everyone has their own restroom. All the other floors have a communal kitchen, and as part of their labor, they also have to cook for everyone else, depending on what's on the menu. All of it is student ran so there is drama, but we do report to a main office.
Management is pretty good but some amenities limited to when office is open
not hate but we do have a $8 fee and they collect our trash outside our door for us. Halls are a little mysterious and dark but it’s chill
Instagram Leasing Agent @blessyouwithalease. Spacious comes with living room private bathroom and Washer in dryer in the same room
10$ double room occupancy. It’s been good 👍
Apartments.com, no hidden fees. Fully furnished, nice appliances, >1000 sq feet, Dw/D included, Hardwood Floors, all utilities except for electricity included, 10 minute walk to campus
No hidden fees but rent is increasing because of renovations.. Pretty good for the cost but theres a roach problem.
We got a deal for 175 off our rent! so we were really enticed to sign quickly around the halloween time. Haven't lived there but excited to with friends!
The rooms (besides the bedrooms) are fairly spacious and we often host a lot of people comfortably
Wanted to just sign with friends near the engineering area. There is a pretty bad cockroach problem so we have to kill them everyday
Apartments.com. It’s only bad bc a little far from campus, but there is a direct bus route which takes 25 mins
It’s new. Brand new nice amenities close to campus
thought a friend, nah. we had water issues for a bit but it’s fine now I like my room
Great place to live overall. Clean, nice, new
Just randomly. Nothing to complain about

Floor 23. It’s nice. The amenities are really nice (Community Study Areas, Private Meeting Areas, Theatre Space, Gaming Space, Basketball Court, Boxing Area, Golf Simulator, Spin Studio, Gym, Makers Space (Art/Crafts), Dog Park, Dog Spa/Wash). Hidden Fees: Rent Service Fee? (It’s like ≈6 a month), another 9% service fee for utilities. Like— the rent is already sky high, wdym you need “service fee”?? Why is it not built in?😭😭😭😭 the rent is enough to cover “services” bruh. I like the Trash Chute, each floor can throw trash easily. Residents aren’t really respectful with it though, not a building problem, it’s a people problem. Wall noise cancelation is good. Front door and window noise cancellation is not, I hear cars screeching to a stop and sirens everyday. The counter/cabinets materia is cheap wood, it’s stick wallpaper type sh.
originally thought it was 1460, changed to 1540 when signing. nice
Had a friend refer me here. Great middle of the road place.

- Found through a leasing agent so shout out Dat! But we did check out alot of places like Toured block and quarters.. My Bathroom is attached to my room and there's not too many amenities so a gym and a lobby with some broken games but we have a roof with a patio! So good for the price
Fantastic, love the amenities, maintenance is decently responsive

"Green fee", "convenience fee" for paying rent on the website (the only place you can pay it), fee for being on a higher level. Usually at least 1 elevator is broken (3 total for 18 floors plus underground parking), some people got moved into a hotel for a month because of the pool renovations that have been going on all year causing water damage and when they came back stuff was broken

Found online when looking for places near engineering side of campus. Application fee was atrocious and couldn’t get that waived when we signed-should’ve waited. Not bad overall but small things-stove slightly tilted. Thermostat only heats cools to one temperature (not a range). Amenities are nice, only real plus.
It was fine. Only thing was the AC condensation was designed to drip into my bathtub. I’d have to get on my hands and knees to scrub off the mineral deposits from it.
Pipes exploded on 8th floor after they hired Juan The Builder

Saw it being built from my old apartment and wanted newer facilities. I don’t think there were any “gotcha” moments for me.. Elevators are always broken, maintenance is a bit mean when asking to take shoes off, otherwise it’s overall a good experience.
No hidden fees!. I haven’t had any problems living here! Honestly one of the better apartments in west campus that I’ve lived at.

1 of the rooms is technically a loft bedroom (no door + upstairs). Found it from a facebook group post from someone looking for a roommate!. Quiet street and decently close to campus. Unit is very outdated but maintenance is quick, water is included in rent, and parking is free. Unit is also unfurnished.
Word of mouth. No hidden fees yet at least.. Good amenities and food

Management is great and maintenance is super quick to fix things. I’ve really loved living here but my only complaint is that the walls are super thin and all of the furniture/cabinets is super cheaply made. They have really good deals for you to resign with them. My first year lease was 1075 but now I pay 999. There’s lots of frat houses near here so you WILL hear them when they have parties. I can sometimes also hear parties coming from upstairs. I’ve only spotted nats since the two years I’ve stayed here but overall pretty free of bugs. 15 minute walk from campus. I believe SMART housing gets a 150 dollar discount but with new management they’re taking it away from some units like mine :\
Lots of little (and big) structural issues that have had to be taken care of. Let me know if you want the full details 👀👀
Look around at different apartments and pick it cause we thought it was the cheapest relatively to other places near campus
My rent is being reduced by $130 next year for resigning
Lots of utilities, secure apartment, away from Wampus, great management
It’s a sorority house and I'm living in the house paying 8000 for room board and dues
Private balcony and it's pretty close to Campus! asked around with people who lived there and they all said it was nice. I also have a private bathroom!
